_comment: CPU Resource Isolation Experiment v1. Controlled variable: COMPUTE (CPU resource limits).
_rationale: Storage IOPS throttling is not achievable with the rancher.io/local-path provisioner in Kind. This experiment uses CPU resource limits as the controlled variable instead. CPU limits are kernel-enforced (cgroup CFS scheduler), genuinely observable in application latency, and accurately described here. Infrastructure A has 2000m CPU limit; Infrastructure B has 200m CPU limit (10x more restricted).
name: cpu-resource-isolation-v1
description: Measures application-visible performance impact of a 10x CPU resource limit difference between Infrastructure A (2000m CPU) and Infrastructure B (200m CPU). Tests whether Kubernetes cgroup CPU throttling on Infrastructure B produces statistically detectable latency increases in a storage-bound workload. Controlled variable: COMPUTE. Storage paths are identical between A and B.

workload.description: Deterministic PRNG-seeded write/read/delete workload exercising /data (PVC-backed) inside each pod. CPU-bound operations (crypto.randomBytes, SHA256, PRNG) amplify the latency impact of CPU throttling.

replication.description: 5 paired trials (A and B executed with the same seed per pair). Seed advances by 1000 per pair for workload variety.

infrastructureB.constraintMechanism: Kubernetes cgroup CFS CPU quota (cpu.cfs_quota_us via cpu resource limit). This is kernel-enforced, not advisory.

storageThrottlingNote: STORAGE THROTTLING IS NOT IMPLEMENTED. Both StorageClasses (standard and standard-throttled) use rancher.io/local-path with parameters:{} and are functionally identical. The storage path /data is the same in both pods. The only controlled infrastructure difference is the CPU resource limit.
hypotheses: Infrastructure B (200m CPU limit) will exhibit higher p95/p99 latency than Infrastructure A (2000m CPU limit) due to CFS scheduler throttling of CPU-bound workload operations.
The latency difference will replicate consistently across 5 paired trials with the same workload definition.

successCriteria.note: With n=5, the test is valid but has limited power. A significant result at alpha=0.05 with n=5 requires a large effect size (Cohen's d > 1.5). Results will be reported honestly regardless of significance.
